_note: Closed registry of engagement classes for the security division. It is the offensive-action analogue of scripts/agent-tools.json: a security agent declares an `engagement:` class in its frontmatter, and CI checks required policy phrases. It does not authenticate an authority reference, verify signatures, classify behavior reliably or enforce host actions. A class declaration is NOT authorization — the operator's written mandate, scope, and applicable law still decide whether an engagement may run. Classes are listed in ascending order of the harm an unauthorized action could cause.

passive-analysis.summary: Reads code, configuration, logs, artifacts, or open sources and produces findings, reports, or designs. Does not touch a live target system.

active-defensive.summary: Interacts with live systems to defend, harden, monitor, or contain only where the operator has an explicit mandate. Ownership alone is insufficient; changes require applicable authorization and change control.

authorized-offensive.summary: Simulates an adversary against explicitly authorized targets. Repository policy requires prior written authorization and a defined scope; the declaration grants no authority.

own_assets.why: an active-defensive agent must state it acts only on assets the operator owns or is contracted to protect

change_control.why: an agent that can change production state must state it works under change control

written_authorization.why: an offensive agent must require prior written authorization

scope_boundary.why: an offensive agent must operate strictly within an agreed scope

stop_condition.why: an offensive agent must define when to stop or escalate rather than press on

any_of: do not cause denial of service
no_destruction.why: an offensive agent must not cause denial of service or destroy data outside explicit, controlled authorization

not_authorization.why: every intrusive class must state that its own declaration is not authorization
